global_logic.tempo_rule: Use a controlled eccentric and full pain-free range of motion; no fixed eccentric duration is required.
global_logic.ordering_rule: Start with the priority compound, then alternate non-competing regions before returning to a muscle.
global_logic.effort_rule: Keep compounds at 1-2 RIR. Keep isolations at 0-2 RIR; failure is optional only on a stable final isolation set.
global_logic.progression_rule: Double progression: add reps within the range, then add the smallest practical load once all prescribed sets reach the top of the range at the target RIR.

LOW_INC_DB_PRESS.name: Low Incline DB Press
technique: Set the bench to 15-30 degrees and lightly retract the shoulder blades.
Lower the dumbbells under control to a comfortable deep stretch.
Press up and slightly inward without turning the movement into a shoulder press.
mistakes: Flaring elbows fully to the sides.
Bouncing or shortening the bottom range.
LOW_INC_DB_PRESS.visualization: Bicep to Pec: Drive the inner biceps toward the upper chest.
LOW_INC_DB_PRESS.proTip: This is the first lift because chest is the priority; preserve the highest-quality sets here.

INC_MACH_PR.name: Incline Machine Press
technique: Set the seat so handles line up with the upper chest.
Keep the ribcage and upper back fixed into the pad.
Use a controlled stretch and press without rolling the shoulders forward.
mistakes: Setting the handles too high and turning it into a shoulder press.
Losing the stretched position.
INC_MACH_PR.visualization: Hug the Ceiling: Press up and slightly inward as if hugging something overhead.
INC_MACH_PR.proTip: A stable alternative when dumbbells are unavailable or their setup limits effort.

REVERSE_HACK_SQUAT.name: Reverse Hack Squat
technique: Brace against the pad and use a stance that lets the knees travel comfortably forward.
Descend under control into the deepest pain-free knee flexion.
Drive through the whole foot without snapping the knees into lockout.
mistakes: Cutting depth or allowing the pelvis to tuck painfully.
Turning each rep into a hip-dominant good morning.
REVERSE_HACK_SQUAT.visualization: Elevator Descent: Let the hips travel down while the knees travel forward.
REVERSE_HACK_SQUAT.proTip: Keep this as the primary squat pattern while it is pain-free and progressing; pendulum is an option, not an upgrade.

PENDULUM_SQUAT.name: Pendulum Squat
technique: Use a stable shoulder-width stance with the feet low enough to allow knee travel.
Descend under control into deep, pain-free knee flexion.
Drive through the mid-foot while keeping the pelvis stable.
mistakes: Cutting depth to add load.
Locking the knees hard at the top.
PENDULUM_SQUAT.visualization: Piston Cue: Let the femurs compress a spring at the bottom.
PENDULUM_SQUAT.proTip: Use this only if it is at least as comfortable and progressive as your reverse hack.

HACK_SQUAT.name: Hack Squat
technique: Keep the back fully supported and use a quad-biased foot position.
Lower under control without the hips curling off the pad.
Press through the whole foot to a soft lockout.
mistakes: Placing the feet so high that the movement becomes predominantly hip-dominant.
Bouncing from the bottom.
HACK_SQUAT.visualization: Elevator Shaft: Let the torso move straight down and up.
HACK_SQUAT.proTip: A valid substitute, not inherently better or worse than reverse hack or pendulum.

LEG_PRESS.name: Leg Press
technique: Use a low-to-mid, shoulder-width foot position for a quad bias.
Lower until just before the pelvis tucks or the low back rounds.
Press through the mid-foot without hard knee lockout.
mistakes: Letting the pelvis roll up from the pad.
Using a short range to chase load.
LEG_PRESS.visualization: Push the Earth: Drive the sled away while staying pinned to the pad.
LEG_PRESS.proTip: A useful quad-pattern alternative if the squat machines are busy or uncomfortable.

CABLE_FLY.name: Cable Fly
technique: Set the pulleys near chest height and keep a soft, fixed elbow bend.
Allow the upper arms to travel into a controlled chest stretch.
Bring the arms together by squeezing the upper arms toward the midline.
mistakes: Bending and extending the elbows like a press.
Letting the shoulders roll forward at the stretch.
CABLE_FLY.visualization: Barrel Hug: Wrap the arms around a large tree.
CABLE_FLY.proTip: It follows the non-competing squat slot so the chest is locally rested after the first press.

MACH_LATERAL.name: Machine Lateral Raise
technique: Keep the torso fixed and lead the movement with the elbows.
Raise into the most controlled pain-free range.
Lower without shrugging or using momentum.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
Jerking the first half of the rep.
MACH_LATERAL.visualization: Puppet Strings: Imagine the elbows are being pulled out to the walls.
MACH_LATERAL.proTip: Direct lateral-delt work matters more for shoulder width than adding more front-delt pressing.

CABLE_LATERAL.name: Cable Lateral Raise
technique: Stand side-on to a low pulley with a slight elbow bend.
Lead with the elbow and raise without torso sway.
Control the loaded bottom stretch.
mistakes: Using body English.
Shrugging or raising far past the controlled range.
CABLE_LATERAL.visualization: Reach for the Walls: Sweep the elbows outward, not upward.
CABLE_LATERAL.proTip: A good alternative if the machine is busy and you can keep the cable path stable.

DB_LATERAL.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
technique: Use a soft elbow bend and a slight torso lean if comfortable.
Lead with the elbows and control the lowering phase.
Keep the traps quiet.
mistakes: Swinging the dumbbells.
Turning the top of each rep into a shrug.
DB_LATERAL.visualization: Scarecrow Arms: The elbows move wide while the hands stay quiet.
DB_LATERAL.proTip: Use this when cables and the lateral-raise machine are unavailable.

LEG_EXTENSION.name: Leg Extension
technique: Align the knee with the machine pivot and lock the hips into the seat.
Extend smoothly and squeeze the quads at the top.
Lower into a full comfortable bend without kicking.
mistakes: Using momentum or lifting the hips from the seat.
Shortening the loaded bottom range.
LEG_EXTENSION.visualization: Glue Cue: Keep the pelvis super-glued to the seat.
LEG_EXTENSION.proTip: This adds knee-extension volume with little systemic fatigue; it is not a mandatory pre-exhaustion exercise.

CABLE_OH_EXT.name: Overhead Cable Extension
technique: Keep the elbows near the ears and the torso braced.
Allow a controlled stretch behind the head.
Extend without turning the rep into a shoulder movement.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows excessively.
Arching the low back to finish the rep.
CABLE_OH_EXT.visualization: Throwing the Ball: Extend the rope as if throwing a medicine ball overhead.
CABLE_OH_EXT.proTip: The overhead position gives the long head of the triceps a useful lengthened stimulus.

RDL_BARBELL.name: Romanian Deadlift
technique: Unlock the knees slightly and push the hips back.
Keep the bar close to the legs and the spine neutral.
End the descent when hip travel stops, then squeeze the glutes to return.
mistakes: Squatting the load down.
Chasing depth by rounding the low back.
RDL_BARBELL.visualization: Car Door: Close a car door behind you with the hips.
RDL_BARBELL.proTip: It is first because it is the most technical and systemically demanding lift of Pull A.

DB_RDL.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
technique: Hold the dumbbells close to the thighs.
Push the hips back with softly unlocked knees.
Stop at the deepest stable hamstring stretch.
mistakes: Bending the knees enough to turn it into a squat.
Rounding the spine for extra depth.
DB_RDL.visualization: Drinking Bird: Tip from the hips with a rigid torso.
DB_RDL.proTip: A practical alternative when the barbell setup is unavailable.

SMITH_RDL.name: Smith Machine RDL
technique: Stand close enough that the bar stays over the mid-foot.
Hinge back while keeping the bar close to the legs.
Finish with the glutes, not spinal extension.
mistakes: Standing so far away that the bar pulls forward.
Rounding or overextending the back.
SMITH_RDL.visualization: Iron Rail: Hinge around a fixed bar path.
SMITH_RDL.proTip: A stable alternative when a fixed path feels better for hamstring loading.

NEUTRAL_PULLUP.name: Weighted Pull-Up
technique: Use a neutral grip and start by depressing the shoulders.
Drive the elbows down toward the hips.
Use a controlled full hang that your shoulders tolerate.
mistakes: Kipping or shortening the bottom range.
Letting the elbows drift far behind the torso.
NEUTRAL_PULLUP.visualization: Elbows to Pockets: Drive the elbows into the back pockets.
NEUTRAL_PULLUP.proTip: The vertical pull alternates with the hinge so the posterior chain gets time before direct curls.

LAT_PULLDOWN.name: Lat Pulldown
technique: Lock the thighs under the pad and begin from a full controlled stretch.
Pull the elbows down toward the hips.
Keep the torso mostly upright with only a modest lean.
mistakes: Turning the movement into a row with excessive lean.
Yanking with the biceps.
LAT_PULLDOWN.visualization: Bend the Bar: Pull the bar around the upper chest.
LAT_PULLDOWN.proTip: A vertical-pull alternative when weighted pull-ups are not the best choice that day.

SEATED_L_CURL.name: Seated Leg Curl
technique: Lock the thigh pad firmly and keep the hips down.
Curl through a controlled full range.
Return slowly into the long hamstring position.
mistakes: Lifting the hips or losing pad contact.
Using momentum at the bottom.
SEATED_L_CURL.visualization: Dig a Trench: Pull the heels back and under the seat.
SEATED_L_CURL.proTip: It complements the RDL by training knee flexion with the hip flexed.

CS_ROW.name: Chest-Supported Row
technique: Keep the chest on the pad throughout the set.
Allow controlled shoulder-blade movement at the stretch.
Pull with the elbows and avoid curling the handles.
mistakes: Lifting the chest from the pad.
Cranking the neck to finish reps.
CS_ROW.visualization: Wrap Around the Pad: Let the upper back wrap around the pad at the bottom.
CS_ROW.proTip: Chest support limits low-back fatigue after RDLs while letting the back work hard.

WIDE_CABLE_ROW.name: Wide Grip Cable Row
technique: Stay upright and pull high and wide with the elbows.
Let the shoulder blades move through a controlled stretch and squeeze.
Keep the torso still.
mistakes: Pulling the elbows into the sides and changing the bias.
Rocking the torso.
WIDE_CABLE_ROW.visualization: Scarecrow Pull: Pull the elbows apart and back.
WIDE_CABLE_ROW.proTip: This complements the lat pulldown by giving Pull B an upper-back horizontal pull.

REV_PEC_DECK.name: Reverse Pec Deck
technique: Set the handles at shoulder height and keep the torso fixed.
Move the arms out and back with a soft, fixed elbow bend.
Control the return without turning it into a row.
mistakes: Using a big scapular row to move the load.
Swinging the torso.
REV_PEC_DECK.visualization: Push the Walls Away: Move the backs of the hands outward.
REV_PEC_DECK.proTip: Direct rear-delt work balances the pressing volume without adding another compound.

FACE_PULL.name: Face Pull
technique: Set the rope high enough to pull toward the forehead.
Finish with the hands apart and a controlled external rotation.
Keep the load modest and the torso still.
mistakes: Pulling to the chin or neck.
Using body swing to move weight.
FACE_PULL.visualization: Double Biceps: Finish in a relaxed double-biceps position.
FACE_PULL.proTip: Use this for rear delts and shoulder comfort, not as a heavy strength lift.

INC_DB_CURL.name: Incline DB Curl
technique: Set the bench to a comfortable incline and let the arms hang back.
Keep the upper arm mostly still while curling and supinating.
Control the long-length bottom position.
mistakes: Swinging the elbows forward.
Cutting the bottom range short.
INC_DB_CURL.visualization: Elbows in Cement: The elbows hinge but do not travel forward.
INC_DB_CURL.proTip: This provides a lengthened biceps stimulus; preacher curls later give a different resistance profile.

PREACHER_CURL.name: Preacher Curl
technique: Set the seat so the upper arm stays firmly on the pad.
Control the lower range and curl without lifting the shoulder.
Use a load that respects the bottom position.
mistakes: Lifting the elbow off the pad.
Dropping rapidly into extension.
PREACHER_CURL.visualization: Hinge Cue: The elbow is a hinge and the upper arm stays fixed.
PREACHER_CURL.proTip: It complements, rather than replaces, the incline curl by loading the biceps differently.

HIGH_INC_SMITH.name: High Incline Smith Press
technique: Set a high incline that still lets the upper chest contribute comfortably.
Lower the bar toward the upper chest or collarbone area.
Press in the fixed path without losing the upper-back setup.
mistakes: Setting the bench so high that it becomes only a shoulder press.
Bouncing the bar from the chest.
HIGH_INC_SMITH.visualization: Scrape the Chin: Position the bench so the bar travels close to the chin on the way down.
HIGH_INC_SMITH.proTip: This is first on Push B because upper-chest pressing is the priority of that day.

SEATED_DB_OHP.name: Seated DB OHP
technique: Set the bench to about 75-80 degrees and brace the torso.
Lower the dumbbells to a comfortable shoulder-level stretch.
Press without excessive low-back arching.
mistakes: Turning it into an incline chest press by reclining or arching.
Using partial reps to chase load.
SEATED_DB_OHP.visualization: Head Through the Window: Bring the head slightly through the arms near the top.
SEATED_DB_OHP.proTip: Two quality sets preserve direct anterior-delt and overhead strength work without displacing chest priority.

TRI_PUSHDOWN.name: Triceps Pushdown
technique: Keep the elbows near the ribs and the shoulders quiet.
Extend fully while separating the rope at the bottom if comfortable.
Control the return.
mistakes: Leaning bodyweight onto the rope.
Moving the elbows forward and back.
TRI_PUSHDOWN.visualization: Break the Rope: Separate the rope as the elbows extend.
TRI_PUSHDOWN.proTip: This gives the triceps a shortened-position complement to overhead extensions.

STANDING_CALF_RAISE.name: Standing Calf Raise
technique: Keep the knees straight but not aggressively locked.
Lower into a deep, pain-free dorsiflexion stretch with control.
Rise by pressing through the big toe and pause briefly at the top.
mistakes: Bouncing from the stretched position.
Using a short range or bending the knees into a seated-calf pattern.
STANDING_CALF_RAISE.visualization: Reach Tall: Push the floor away through the big toe and grow tall at the top.
STANDING_CALF_RAISE.proTip: Standing work is the one calf exercise because it is the best single choice for gastrocnemius and whole-calf growth; your calves are maintained, not prioritized.
